triage.note: Seven ways the D5 half-1 layout regresses, one failure each, at an EXACT count so both a regressed miss (too few) and a regressed over-fire (too many) go red — the S5 pane-heights-ragged idiom. The seven: (1) the base `.split` rule loses a track, i.e. 'narrower columns' taken as 'one fewer pane', which stacks nothing and still hides the compare pane at every width; (2) the stacking `@media` re-raised to the pre-D5 1100px — the original V5 defect, restored verbatim; (3) the JS still watches `matchMedia("(max-width:1000px)")`, so between 1001 and 1100 the panes stack under a control that has not been told, which is the ORIGINAL V5 complaint (a live-looking control with nothing to sync) reintroduced through the gap between two numbers rather than through either one; (4) `syncOn()` drops the `!c.disabled` term, so a disabled control still drives the sync and disabling it changes only its appearance; (5) `syncStacked()` disables the control but sets no `#sync-state` wording; (6) the `change` listener is gone, so the state is evaluated once at load and a resize past the breakpoint leaves it stale; (7) the `#sync-state` element itself is gone. Every OTHER hop in the fixture is correctly wired.
triage.ceiling: Same static-read ceiling as ui-split-breakpoint: this fixture is a text file, and the check reads text. It proves the CHECK catches these seven source shapes; it says nothing about what any browser renders.
